portInfo.description: Ponta Delgada on São Miguel is the Azores’ main large-ship cruise call. Portos dos Açores identifies Terminal Marítimo das Portas do Mar as one of only two dedicated passenger/cruise terminals in the archipelago (with Horta), in service since 2008, and notes that the largest ships can also use the commercial quay. The Azores Cruise port sheet (Visit Azores / ATA) publishes Portas do Mar dimensions (360 m line, 340 m ships, 11 m depth, 9.2 m max draught) and a 200 m downtown figure, plus commercial-port alternatives. Portas do Mar also hosts leisure/commercial waterfront facilities under Portos dos Açores management.

climate.description: Oceanic climate with mild temperatures year-round

politics.visaRequirements: Entry and visa rules depend on nationality. Many visitors use Schengen short-stay rules, but requirements change—confirm with official government sources and your cruise line before travel.
politics.entryRequirements: Carry a valid passport (or a national ID where your cruise line and destination authorities accept it). Cruise transit formalities can differ from a normal airport entry—follow your ship’s document list.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Terminal Marítimo das Portas do Mar — Av. Infante D. Henrique, 9500-767 Ponta Delgada
gettingThere.distanceToCity: ~200 m to downtown from Portas do Mar per Azores Cruise sheet; taxis and bus parking listed among general services. Airport ~5 km. Exact door-to-Praça walk metres still null beyond the sheet claim.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Portas do Mar waterfront / city centre — walk.
Portas da Cidade (city gates) — short stroll inland.
Sete Cidades or Furnas — half-day road trips; only with confirmed timing.
Pineapple plantation / tea estate tours — island specialities; book buffers.
Portas do Mar waterfront / city gates area
thingsToDo.shortCall: Stay near the port area and keep a generous buffer before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.standardCall: Combine a central walk, one attraction, and lunch if times allow—start back well before all-aboard.
thingsToDo.longerCall: A second stop or coach outing is realistic only with confirmed transport and an eight-hour or longer window.
thingsToDo.practicalTip: If assigned the commercial quay, budget the extra ~2 km to centre versus Portas do Mar.
